What is zero trust architecture and how do you implement it in a real enterprise?

Zero Trust (ZT) principle: 'Never trust, always verify' — no implicit trust based on network location. Every access request authenticated, authorized, and encrypted regardless of source. NIST SP 800-207 components: 1) Identity: strong MFA for all users and devices. Identity as the new perimeter. SAML/OIDC/OAuth for federated identity. Privileged Identity Management (PAM) for admin accounts. 2) Device: device health verification before access. MDM compliance checks. Certificate-based device identity (not just user identity). 3) Network: microsegmentation — separate east-west traffic by application, not just perimeter firewalls. Software-Defined Perimeter (SDP). Encrypted communications everywhere (mTLS). 4) Application: application-layer access policies. App-level authentication (BeyondCorp model). CASB for cloud apps. 5) Data: DLP, data classification, encryption at rest. Policy enforcement at data layer. Implementation pathway: 1) Identify your 'protect surface' (most critical data/systems). 2) Map transaction flows to those assets. 3) Build ZT architecture around protect surface. 4) Create ZT policy (who/what/when/where/how). 5) Monitor and maintain. Common mistakes: boiling the ocean (trying to ZT everything at once), ignoring legacy systems, not accounting for OT/IoT, treating ZT as purely a technology project rather than an architecture.
